edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. in Cant. Prologus 7

source_text: Est autem duplex homo: exterior et interior. Exterior homo de terrae limo factus est; interior ad imaginem Dei. Exterioris amores carnales sunt; interioris amores spiritales. Canticum Canticorum non de exteriore, sed de interiore loquitur — de anima quae Verbum amat et ab eo amatur. Nisi quis se noverit interiorem, nescit quid in hoc libro quaerat.
pass_a_gloss: There-is however twofold human: outer and inner. Outer human from earth's mud made is; inner unto image of-God. Of-outer loves carnal are; of-inner loves spiritual. Song of-Songs not about outer but about inner speaks — about soul which Word loves and by-him is-loved...
pass_b_english: But the human being is twofold: outer and inner. The outer human was made from the mud of the earth; the inner according to the image of God. The loves of the outer are carnal; the loves of the inner spiritual. The Song of Songs speaks not of the outer but of the inner — of the soul that loves the Word and is loved by him. Unless someone knows himself or herself as inner, that person does not know what to seek in this book.
